evals.name: receiving-cost
evals.prompt: Write a short receiving guide for new operators of the fictional Brindle inventory app using these notes and verified behavior. Return only the guide. Rough note: Enter stock, check units and cost, resolve any problems, post receipt. Verified behavior: Items > select item > Receive existing stock contains Quantity and Cost (per stock unit). The item Flour uses grams as its stock unit. A supplier sack contains 6 kg and costs $72 total. Convert the sack to the stock unit when entering both fields. Blank cost is stored as zero. Before Post, the operator can correct either field directly. Once posted there is no edit or undo; give the receipt ID to the inventory lead for an audited correction. The posted row is visible in Items > select item > History with quantity, stock unit, unit cost and receipt ID. There is no cost-unit selector.
evals.expected_output: Usable, faithful prose that satisfies the task without invented details.
assertions: The guide names the receiving location and enters 6000 grams and $0.012 per gram, with cost per stock unit distinguished from total sack cost.
The check has observable fields and expected values, with correction before Post and a warning that blank cost becomes zero.
After posting, it uses the History receipt ID and inventory lead for audited correction; it invents neither an undo nor a cost-unit selector.

evals.name: migration-coverage
evals.prompt: Rewrite this fictional Brindle migration page into a concise useful guide. Use current evidence to resolve stale text; return only the guide, no editing commentary. Original: Before migration, export a backup and confirm the destination workspace name on the Apply screen. Applying cannot be undone. CSV import creates opening quantities, not past transactions. Opening quantities do not retain source lot labels or expiry dates. Later receipts do not retroactively identify those opening units. Keep the source records for recalls and expiry tracking of opening stock. Old restriction: comments cannot be imported. Choose CSV under Import, preview the item and quantity rows, then Apply. Current evidence confirms every statement except the comments restriction: comments are now imported in the Comment column. No other behavior has changed.
evals.expected_output: Usable, faithful prose that satisfies the task without invented details.
assertions: It preserves backup, destination confirmation and irreversible Apply warning near the action.
It preserves missing past transactions AND the distinct lot-label and expiry-date loss for opening quantities.
It preserves that later receipts cannot retroactively identify opening units and says to keep source records for recalls/expiry tracking.
It uses the current Comment-column support rather than retaining the obsolete comments restriction and keeps the supported CSV preview/apply path.

evals.name: conditional-recovery
evals.prompt: Turn these messy fictional Larch shop-connector notes into an onboarding page. Return only the page. Verified source: First Connections > Add shop, authorize the desired shop, then Import products. Next open Connections > Products and review Mapping status. A Mapped row is ready; do not remap it. Only an Unmatched row needs Link item and selection of the corresponding inventory item. If no inventory item exists, ask the inventory lead to create it before linking that row. Product import does not start order sync: press Start sync after all rows are mapped. Only if Connections > Account shows the wrong shop, Disconnect and authorize the correct shop, then reimport. Only if sync status is Authorization expired, select Reauthorize; this is not a routine setup step. Old notes currently mix disconnecting, relinking every row and reauthorizing into the numbered setup list.
evals.expected_output: Usable, faithful prose that satisfies the task without invented details.
assertions: The normal sequence is authorize, import, review mappings, Start sync after all mapped; import alone does not start sync.
It gives Mapping status location, Mapped/Unmatched conditions, and Link item or inventory-lead remedy only for Unmatched rows.
Disconnect/reimport and Reauthorize are clearly conditional on wrong shop and Authorization expired respectively, not universal prerequisites.

evals.name: coverage-audit
evals.prompt: Review this fictional Cedar task-import rewrite against its original and current evidence. Give only consequential fixes and replacement wording; no full rewrite. Original: Back up the destination and confirm the workspace on Apply. Apply cannot be undone. A matching TaskCode overwrites the existing task fields. Comments, attachments and archived tasks cannot be imported. Draft: Select CSV under Import, preview the rows, and press Apply. Comments are supported. Import history is limited. Current evidence: Comment-column import now works. Attachments and archived tasks remain unsupported. TaskCode matching still overwrites existing fields, Apply remains irreversible, and backup plus destination confirmation are still prerequisites. Do not rely on any behavior outside this evidence.
evals.expected_output: Usable, faithful prose that satisfies the task without invented details.
assertions: The review restores backup, workspace confirmation and irreversible Apply warning.
It restores matching TaskCode overwrite behavior rather than accepting a generic history warning as equivalent.
It names both unsupported attachments and archived tasks without restoring the stale comments restriction.
It supplies actionable replacement wording and does not invent new UI or mechanisms.

evals.name: literary-control
evals.prompt:
Proofread only for spelling errors. If there are none, return the passage unchanged, without quotation marks or commentary.

By six, the garden had gone blue. My father kept digging—slowly, as if the potatoes might object. We ate late; nobody mentioned the clock.
evals.expected_output: Usable, faithful prose that satisfies the task without invented details.
assertions: It returns the passage exactly, preserving punctuation, wording, and paragraph without procedural additions or commentary.
